# P060 · Prescription Rules (P-series)

Single-rule view — the full series catalog lives at [`prescriptions.md`](../prescriptions.md#p060).

Suppress a finding on the violating line or the line directly above it:

```python
# conformance: ignore[P060] intentional: <why this is deliberate here>
```

## P060 — `HandRolledRetryLadder` {#p060}

**Tier:** `warn` · **Scope:** `sdk` · **Category:** `retry-policy` · **Autofixable:** — · **Since:** 0.54.0

> Hand-rolled retry ladder — a loop with try/except and a sleep, outside application_sdk.common.backoff

**Rationale:** Every hand-rolled retry loop picks its own delay arithmetic and its own jitter, and the
conventions drift: before FND-4284 the SDK had three jitter schemes across about a dozen
ladders and five with no jitter at all. An un-jittered ladder makes every worker that
lost the same dependency retry in lockstep, a fleet-wide retry storm against the
dependency that is trying to recover. One helper, application_sdk.common.backoff, owns
the arithmetic and the jitter so they cannot drift again.

Flags a `sleep` call inside a `for` / `while` / `async for` loop whose body also holds a
`try` statement with at least one `except` handler — the shape of a hand-rolled retry
ladder.  Both may sit at any depth inside the loop (the sleep in the `except` block is
the commonest spelling), but not inside a nested function, lambda or class, which runs
on its own schedule.  The finding is reported at the **sleep call's** line, once per
sleep call, so the suppression comment sits next to the delay it justifies.

Sleep calls matched: `asyncio.sleep(...)`, `time.sleep(...)`, `anyio.sleep(...)` (also
through an `import ... as` alias), and a bare `sleep(...)` imported from one of those
modules.

Not flagged:

* `application_sdk/common/backoff.py` itself — it is the one loop allowed to walk a
  ladder.
* `asyncio.sleep(0)` — the yield-to-the-event-loop idiom, not a delay.
* a loop that sleeps but has no `try`/`except` — a plain poller or periodic flush loop
  has nothing to retry.
* `workflow.sleep(...)` — a durable Temporal timer, not an in-process delay.

Fix: express the ladder as a `Backoff` and hand the call to
`application_sdk.common.backoff.retry_async(call, backoff=..., retry_if=...)`.  A loop
with its own control flow — a supervisor that resets its streak, or one racing a
shutdown event — keeps its loop and asks `Backoff.delay(retry)` for the number, so the
arithmetic and the jitter still come from the one helper.

Suppress a loop that is genuinely not a retry ladder (a poller whose `try` only guards a
log call, say) with a justification: `# conformance: ignore[P060] <reason>`.
